originalTitle: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq end higher on cool inflation data, solid bank earnings
simplifiedContent: Today, the US stock market had a good day, with two important groups of stocks, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, ending with higher values. This happened because inflation (the rate at which prices are rising) was not as high as expected in June, and some big banks like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs reported strong earnings. This news made investors feel more positive, even though there are worries about tensions in the Middle East. As a result, investors now think it's less likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates soon, which also helped the market. The Nasdaq did especially well, thanks to gains in the computer chip industry.

originalTitle: US derivatives regulator blocks Kalshi from canceling Michigan trades despite court order
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: a company called Kalshi had been making sports-related trades in Michigan, but a state court told them to stop because these trades are considered a form of gambling. However, a US regulator that oversees these types of trades stepped in and said Kalshi can't cancel the trades, even though the state court said they have to. This is creating a conflict between the federal regulator and the state of Michigan, which has bigger implications for how these types of trades are regulated. It's a clash between federal authorities who support these types of trades and states that consider them gambling, which could impact the future of similar trading platforms. This matter raises questions about who gets to decide what is allowed and what is not in the trading world.

originalTitle: Why IBM shares crashed 26%: CEO Arvind Krishna highlights customer spending shifts towards AI
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened: IBM's stock price dropped 26% because the company didn't do as well as expected in the second quarter. This happened because customers are changing how they spend their money, and they're now prioritizing artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. As a result, IBM's sales suffered, especially in areas like mainframe business and hardware. The CEO, Arvind Krishna, said that the company also made some mistakes that contributed to the poor results. This matters because it shows that IBM is struggling to keep up with changing customer needs, which can affect its stock price.

originalTitle: Multibagger Signature Global shares to be in focus on Wednesday after Q1 pre-sales rise 25% QoQ
simplifiedContent: Signature Global is a company that will be closely watched on Wednesday because of its recent sales performance. The company's sales for the first quarter of the financial year 2027 were ₹1,970 crore, which is 25% less than the same time last year, but 25% more than the previous quarter. This increase is partly due to the launch of a new project called Tonino Lamborghini Residences. This news matters because it shows how the company is performing and can affect its stock price. The company's shares may be more active than usual on Wednesday as investors react to this news.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver rebound as softer US inflation eases Fed rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: Gold and silver prices went up on July 14th because inflation in the US wasn't as high as expected. This means that the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) might not increase interest rates as much as people thought, which is good for gold and silver. As a result, the prices of gold and silver increased, with gold reaching $4,112 and silver reaching $60. This change in prices is important because it shows how investors are reacting to the latest economic news. The decrease in inflation and the current tensions in the Middle East are supporting the increase in precious metal prices.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and LIC (a large insurance company) are working together to sell a majority stake in IDBI Bank, which is around 60.72% of the bank's shares. This means they want to find a buyer to take over a significant portion of the bank. The government owns about 30.48% of the bank, while LIC owns around 30.24%, and together they own almost 95% of IDBI Bank. This sale is important because it will give the buyer control over the management of the bank. The process of finding a buyer is moving forward, with the government reviewing new bids from interested parties.
